The error I get in eclipse is:
DnsNameResolverContext cannot be resolved

Although DnsNameResolverContext class is shown in package descriptor but I am unable to import it using import io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsNameResolverContext;
I also tried static import but still does not work.
@jarusgnuj can you build it on the cmd line via mvn ?
Yes I can, but not being able to run it in eclipse.
@jarusgnuj I'm afraid but this means it is an eclipse issue and not a netty usage. You will need to talk to the eclipse community then.

I built a eclipse project in resolver-dns and tried running DnsNameResolverTest with Java 6 but 
I keep getting java.lang.autocloseable error. Is not netty suppose to run on Java 6.

@jarusgnuj oh I see.. it should. this is a bug then.

@trustin could you take a look ?
Hi, Has there been any updates on this?

Not yet, super busy. If you want to speedup things you coukd submit a PR to fix this. i would be happy to review

> Am 25.11.2014 um 03:59 schrieb jarusgnuj notifications@github.com:

> Hi, Has there been any updates on this?
>

> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub.

I found `DnsNameResolver` uses `InetSocketAddress.getHostString()` which is only available since Java 7, and fixed the compatibility issue.  After fixing, I was able to use `DnsNameResolver` in Java 6.

I did not fix `DnsNameResolverTest` because it is meant to run in Java 7+.  If you want to run it on Java 6, you can simply replace `getHostString()` to `getHostName()` then all tests should pass. (I confirmed this.)

Hi Trustin, Thank you for the fix. Although, it is strange that when I run the DnsNameResolverTest I get the java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: java/lang/AutoCloseable exception. Is not Autocloseable only implemented in java 7 and not java 6, thus the exception in java 6.
That's probably because you are running against master.  Use the branch 4.1.
